## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The second piece of the *xuánlíng zhuǎnjīng* triad, transmitted with [KR5b0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0183) and [KR5b0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0185) as 三儀同卷軆八 ("three liturgies in one fascicle, *Tǐ* 8"). The noon *cháo* of the set occupies the central, mediating position in the day's three-fold *xíngdào* 行道 (way-practice) framework.

**Abstract**

The noon *xíngdào* is structurally a *duplicate* of the morning rite (cf. [KR5b0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0183)) — same opening hymn, same dispatch of the celestial messengers, same enumeration of the *qǐngchēng fǎwèi* 請稱法位 — with substitutions reflecting the *zhōng* 中 / *yáng* 陽 position of noon in cosmological hour-symbolism: invocations of the noon-time *Dōnghuá* 東華 powers and of the *Sīmìng* 司命 of the southern (*yáng*) realm. Per Lagerwey (*Taoist Canon* 2: 996–997), the structural redundancy across the three *cháo* is deliberate: it inscribes the cosmic three-fold (morning/noon/evening, Heaven/Earth/Man, *sānyuán* 三元) into the temporal articulation of the *Jīnlù* fast, while the recitation of the *Dùrén jīng* in each *cháo* effects the universal salvific turning of the scripture for the cosmos's three temporal phases.
